newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on NWS weather forecast.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on NWS weather forecast.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook, traders said.

NWS called for normal to below normal temperatures and normal to above normal rainfall in the U.S. Midwest from July 29 to August 2, a scenario that diminished fears about potential harm to the pollinating crop.

Joel Burgio, a meteorologist with Weather Services Corp, said temperatures were expected to peak in the mid-90s Fahrenheit in Nebraska, Missouri and southwest Illinois on Friday and Saturday, with low 90s expected in Peoria, Illinois.
But Burgio said long-range forecasts showed showers and cooler temperatures would reach the Corn Belt by Monday as a front moved across the region.
USDA's weekly export sales report was bearish.
The government Thursday during the week ended July 17, net export sales of old-crop corn totalled 169,900 tonnes, below expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
New export sales of new-crop corn totalled 377,300 tonnes, above expectations for 250,000 to 350,000 tonnes.
Corn closed one to 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with September down 3-3/4 at $2.43-1/2.
Iowa Grain sold four million bushesl of December and bought two million, traders said. Refco Inc sold four million December and bought three million, traders said.

Cargill Inc sold two million bushels of December and Continental Grain sold 2.5 million December and sold 1.5 million September, traders said. Dean Witter Reynolds bought three million bushels of December, traders said.

In spread dealings, Cargill Investor Services did 2.5 million bushels of December/March at eight to 8-1/2 cents, premium March and LIT America did two million December/July at 18 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 43,000 contracts, below the 54,167 traded Wednesday.

In corn options, E.D. and F. Man InternaAional bought 800 December $2.50 calls at 9-3/4 cents, Cargill Investor Services sold 500 December $2.50 calls at 10 to 9-1/2 cents and Smith Barney sold 400 December $2.30 puts at five cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, above the 13,803 traded Wednesday.
